VALLEY GENERAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PROVIDER NOTE

Chief complaint: Right ankle pain after a fall.

HPI: 61 year old woman who stepped off a curb awkwardly this afternoon and inverted her right ankle. Immediate pain and swelling over the lateral ankle. Able to bear weight with difficulty. No head strike, no loss of consciousness, no other injuries. Took ibuprofen 400 mg at home with partial relief.

PMH: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Medications: Amlodipine 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: Sulfa (rash). Patient also reports that in her 30s she developed hives with lip and throat swelling about 30 minutes after a dose of Augmentin prescribed for a sinus infection and was treated with epinephrine in an emergency room. She has not taken it since.
Social: Non-smoker, occasional wine.

Exam: Vitals BP 146/88, HR 84, afebrile. Right ankle with lateral swelling and ecchymosis, tenderness over the ATFL, no tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus, no midfoot tenderness. Neurovascularly intact distally.

Imaging: Not indicated per Ottawa ankle rules.

Assessment: Right lateral ankle sprain, grade I to II.
Plan: RICE, ankle brace, ibuprofen as needed with food, crutches as needed. Follow up with primary care in 1 to 2 weeks if not improving. Return precautions discussed. Discharged in stable condition.

VALLEY GENERAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admission 2026-09-18. Discharge 2026-09-22.
Attending: Dr. H. Adeyemi, Cardiology

Principal diagnosis: Non-ST elevation myocardial infarction.
Secondary diagnoses: Coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Hospital course: 73 year old man presented with 2 hours of substernal chest pressure. Troponin peaked at 4.2 ng/mL. Cardiac catheterization on 9/19 showed a 90% proximal LAD stenosis, treated with a drug-eluting stent. His oral home medications were held for 48 hours after contrast and resumed on 9/21 at home doses. He received a heparin infusion, and pantoprazole 40 mg daily for stress ulcer prophylaxis, during the admission. Echo EF 50%.

Discharge medications: Continue aspirin 81 mg daily indefinitely. Start clopidogrel 75 mg once daily for at least 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy; do not interrupt without speaking to cardiology. Metoprolol succinate ER is increased from 25 mg to 50 mg once daily. Continue atorvastatin 80 mg daily. Start lisinopril 5 mg once daily. Start pantoprazole 40 mg once daily for GI protection while on dual antiplatelet therapy. Continue his other home medications unchanged.

Follow-up: Cardiology in 2 weeks. PCP within 1 week.

notes.author: Lakeside Heart Associates
notes.text:
LAKESIDE HEART ASSOCIATES - CLINIC LETTER

Dear Dr. Okafor,

Thank you for allowing us to share in the care of Mr. O'Brien, whom I saw today for early follow-up after his 9/19 LAD stent. He has no further chest pain and the access site has healed well. Lightheadedness has improved since the lisinopril was stopped.

CYP2C19 genotyping sent during his admission has returned showing he is a poor metabolizer (*2/*2), so clopidogrel will not adequately protect his stent. Today I stopped clopidogrel and started ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily, first dose given in clinic. Please keep aspirin at 81 mg daily (no higher with ticagrelor). All other medications unchanged.

We will see him again in 3 months.

Sincerely,
Dr. N. Osei, Cardiology

Indication: nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Current regimen: apixaban 5 mg twice daily.

VALLEY GENERAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admission 2026-09-24. Discharge 2026-09-28.
Attending: Dr. R. Feld, Hospital Medicine

Principal diagnosis: Hypertensive urgency.
Secondary diagnoses: Hyponatremia, E. coli urinary tract infection, type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia, chronic cough.

Hospital course: 64 year old woman presented with headache and BP 212/118 without evidence of end-organ damage. Admission sodium 128, attributed to hydrochlorothiazide, improved to 133 with fluid restriction and holding the thiazide. Urinalysis on admission showed pyuria and culture grew pan-sensitive E. coli; she received ceftriaxone on 9/24 and 9/25 and was switched to oral cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily on 9/26 to complete a 7-day course, with the final dose due the evening of 9/30. A1c 8.4%. She also reported a dry cough for about 8 months, which her PCP had previously attributed to lisinopril. During the admission she received enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis, insulin lispro correction scale, and pantoprazole 40 mg daily, which was substituted for her home omeprazole per the hospital formulary. BP improved on the regimen below.

Discharge medications: Her lisinopril was discontinued given the persistent dry cough attributed to the ACE inhibitor, and she was started on losartan 50 mg once daily in its place. Hydrochlorothiazide was stopped because of the hyponatremia and should not be restarted. For adherence, her metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily was changed to metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once daily. Metformin was increased to 1000 mg twice daily and empagliflozin 10 mg once daily was added for glycemic control. She should continue aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily, and continue cefpodoxime as above until the course is complete. All other home medications are to be continued unchanged.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. BMP in 1 week to recheck sodium and potassium.

notes.author: Dr. P. Lindqvist, Valley General Hospital
notes.text:
Admission 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-15.

Diagnosis: Acute right lower lobe segmental pulmonary embolism after a long car trip. No right heart strain. Lower extremity ultrasound negative. Sinus rhythm throughout on telemetry.

Anticoagulation: Apixaban 10 mg twice daily through 8/18 (7 days from 8/12), then 5 mg twice daily. Plan at least 3 months of treatment, then reassess duration.

Follow-up: PCP in 3 to 4 weeks.

notes.author: Dr. A. Shah
notes.text: Pulmonary embolism follow-up. Dyspnea resolved. Taking apixaban 5 mg twice daily since 8/19, no bleeding. Wt 56.2 kg. Creatinine 1.54, eGFR 37, at her CKD 3b baseline. Continue anticoagulation and reassess duration at 3 months.

notes.author: Dr. M. Okafor
notes.text: Healthy adult. No chronic conditions. No known drug allergies. Return in 1 year.

notes.author: Dr. M. Okafor
notes.text:
Walk-in visit for sore throat.

HPI: Sudden sore throat and fever to 102 since yesterday, pain with swallowing, no cough. His son was diagnosed with strep 4 days ago.

Vitals: T 38.9 C, HR 102.
Exam: Tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes.

Rapid strep antigen: POSITIVE.

Assessment: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis.
Plan: Antibiotic to be ordered.
